title: Who Called? V33DA: A Physically Verified Multimodal Benchmark for Vocal Attribution in Zebra Finch Groups
claim: A multi-sensor benchmark event is verified across modalities, and embedding geometry shows transferable attribution depends on spatial structure rather than identity.
layout: 9 panels a–i, grid; top sensor panels, bottom row of three UMAPs
description: A dense nine-panel figure. Panel a, at upper left, is a 3D rendering of the aviary (BirdPark). It shows microphones as red triangles, radio antennas as blue arrows, three camera frusta, and colored dots for the birds. A legend sits beside it. Panel b is a four-view camera mosaic with colored dashed borders. Panel c is a close-up crop of a bird with a neon-green ring on its backpack. Panel d shows three accelerometer vibration spectrograms, with blue, orange and red color bars for the three birds. Panel e shows radio telemetry line plots for antennas A–D: baseband power, relative phase and compensation phase. Panel f is a stack of five microphone spectrograms. The bottom row has three UMAP scatter plots. Panel g is the on-body reference, split into silent and vocalizing clusters. Panel h is SELDnet++, colored by bird identity. Panel i is SpatialScorer, colored by position along a gradient. Dataset and Code icons sit at the top.
caption: V33DA overview and representation geometry. a. BirdPark rendering with calibrated microphones, camera poses, the 4-antenna FM receiver array, and triangulated bird positions. b. Synchronized multi-view frame with tracked individuals. c. Candidate-centered crop; the neon-green ring marks the vocalizing bird's backpack. d. Accelerometer-derived vibration spectrograms; left color bars mark the blue, peach, and red birds. e. Per-antenna (A--D) radio telemetry---baseband signal power, relative phase, and compensation phase---over the event, with the same color bars. f. Five-channel microphone spectrograms. Panels a--f show the same verified event across geometry, video, on-body sensing, radio telemetry, and multichannel audio. g. UMAP of withheld on-body reference embeddings: the reference cleanly separates the caller from silent birds. h. SELDnet++ embeddings organized primarily by bird identity. i. SpatialScorer embeddings organized primarily by vocalizer position. Panels g--i preview the main result: transferable attribution depends on spatial organization more than on identity recognition.
abstract: Deciding which member of an animal group produced a vocalization and where that vocalization was produced are central to studying social communication but are rarely evaluated with physically verified ground truth. Existing resources either localize sounds without identifying the caller, or recognize individuals from isolated vocalizations without reliance on the 3D candidate geometry. We close this gap with V33DA, a dataset-centered multimodal benchmark for spatial vocal attribution in social zebra finches: it comprises 33,625 verified events coupling 5-channel audio with three camera views, calibrated 3D pose for every visible candidate, and per-bird radio telemetry across 10 individuals and three experiments. Caller identity is verified from an on-body accelerometer-derived vibration signal; this channel is withheld from benchmark models and used only by an on-body reference ceiling. Given a detected vocalization and the visible candidate birds, the task is to select the caller. We evaluate it under three regimes: session-disjoint testing on familiar birds from held-out recording dates, held-out-experiment transfer to a new cohort, and leave-one-individual-out evaluation on a bird whose vocalizations are held out from training. Reference methods expose a consistent gap between in-domain accuracy and transfer to unseen individuals: methods that can exploit familiar vocal identity perform well on known callers but degrade sharply on unseen ones, whereas candidate-aware methods preserving explicit spatial reasoning transfer substantially better. The on-body reference stays near-perfect across regimes, confirming the internal consistency of the accelerometer-verified labels. We release V33DA with fixed protocols and code for the evaluated methods, and V33DA++, an unevaluated companion set of verified overlapping-call events and +/-2 s context windows.
